meta_description_en: Outlet #013 readers' letters: transferring The Writer to the Plus D disc interface, and quirks and pitfalls of the ZX Spectrum 128 BASIC screen editor.
meta_description_ru: Письма читателей Outlet #013: перенос программы The Writer на дисковый интерфейс Plus D, особенности и подводные камни строчного редактора BASIC в ZX Spectrum 128.

September,1988       Page  Reply

 How to write to us...02     -

 Trevor Wright........03    05

 John Luby............06    11

 Douglas Goldsworthy..13    14

 E.J. Chun............15    19

 Anthony Poli.........20    22

 E.M. Duffield........23    26

      HOW TO WRITE TO OUTLET
      ----------------------
Letters are accepted  in  almost
any form for publication in our
OUTLETTERS: BASIC PRINT or  DATA
statements, handwritten or typed
pages, a simple  JOTTER  program
is provided in Issue 2(Disk #4);
mailbox messages via Prestel No.
014703943 but the easiest for us
to edit are Tasword 2 files with
the right-hand margin set at 32.

Please state if there should  be
parts of your letter you do  not
wish published but we always use
our discretion  anyway.  Letters
may also be edited  for  clarity
and length... Please ask if  you
welcome  direct   correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

Trevor Wright,  Melton Mowbray

Dear Ron and Brian,

Many thanks for all your
splendid work on Outlet which I
enjoy reading and using when I
get the time! What I would like
to do through the pages of
Outlet is appeal for some help.

Having purchased a Plus D
interface a few months ago I
have been busily transferring
all my programs on to disc. One
which is causing me a lot of
trouble is 'The Writer'. I have
managed to transfer it to disc
using the microdrive version but
it refuses to SAVE or LOAD to
disc or load up the help files.

Is there any clever chap or
chapess out there who can help
me?

Hoping there is somebody who can
oblige.

             Yours,

         Trevor Wright.

To: Trevor Wright from Ron

Dear Trevor,

So, The Writer rears it's head
again. As you will realize from
the letters page in issue 012, I
have been getting nowhere with
this program but, like you, I
did manage to save it to disc,
however, I cannot even find the
correct procedure to LOAD a
file.

Although Softechics have failed
to answer Bill Clarke's queries,
maybe this is the way to pursue
it. I'll have a go at contacting
them and let you know how I get
on.
               RON

From John Luby,  Duns

Dear Ron/Brian,

More tips for 128-ers (no charge
-I didn't invent this stuff). I
mentioned last time the way the
128k editing routine tries to
"tokenise" anything that appears
to be a "reserved word" (i.e. a
command or function). Be warned,
it does the reverse when text is
enclosed in quotes. A line like:

 LET p = VAL "PEEK 23606 + 256
 * PEEK 23607"

won't work at all if entered in
128 mode. If entered in 48k
mode, it will work in 128k
unless you edit it, in which

case the editor DE-tokenises
anything in quotes. Also,
"embedded" colour codes aren't
available in 128k mode. 48k
lines with embedded attributes
WILL work (although the effects
can't be seen in 128k listings).
Edit the line, however, and the
codes will disappear. If you're
programming in 128k mode,
attributes have to be added "the
hard way" (PRINT PAPER 2;INK 7
etc). Lastly, tabbing your
listings or text with <EXTEND>,
<6>, <DELETE> is OUT if you want
to list them in 128k. CHR$ 6
does horrible things with 128k
listings, even hanging up in
some cases. You'll just have to
go back to using REMs to space
out your listings, and spaces in

your text! (And I bet you
thought the 128k screen editor
was a step ahead!).

A news item/plea for help:-

An advert in Popular Computing
Weekly a few weeks ago promised
a 3-octave keyboard/ interface/
software for the 128k Spectrum
(+2, +3), for `19.95 inc p&p,
from:
    Omnidale Ltd.,
    23 Curzon Street,
    DERBY DE1 1LH.
    (Tel 0332 291219).

I ordered one, and found it to
be a genuine bargain at the
price. The unit seems to be the
one offered some time ago by

Currys as a bundle with the 128,
and includes a keyboard (with 37
piano-size keys), a connecting
lead, 'ECHO' interface, software
on cassette and instruction
manual. Within its obvious
limitations, the system produces
some nice sounds via the 128. I
had no trouble converting the
software to microdrive, and I'll
be happy to pass on details to
anyone needing help. The
software is, however, the weak
link. It works well enough
considering the price, but I
suspect that the hardware is
capable of a lot more than the
rather simple software allows.
Has anyone out there got any
experience with this piece of
equipment?

Lastly, my thanks to George
Matthews of Barking for
answering my request for help
with a screen dump for the
GP100A. His code didn't actually
solve my problem, so I'm still
looking. (I'm coming to the
conclusion that a new interface
is the answer). It's the thought
that counts, though. Many
thanks, George.
                  John Luby.

P.S: You seem to have fallen
under the spell of the "bouncing
dot" routine I sent you. It
certainly seems either to grab
people or leave them stone cold!
I never tire of it. Do you think
we could get discount on a block
booking for treatment?

To John Luby from Ron

Dear John,

In your letter you have a couple
of tips for 128-ers and, as I am
now searching the country for a
replacement full-stroke (QWERTY)
keyboard, I wondered a) what you
thought of the 128K keyboard and
b) whether it could be linked to
a 48K circuit board (I've just
heard of someone with a burnt-
out 128K and am wondering
whether to buy it cheap for the
keyboard!).

I'm afraid I can't help with
your musical query as I am tone
deaf and can't tell my trumpet
from my oboe so we'll put an

entry in OUTLET and see what
comes up.

Regards, Ron

P.S. I kicked the habit of
"bouncing dot" routines (I've
got a very pretty psychiatrist)
- I'm into "fill" routines now!



[John, If you can send a photo-
copy of the relevant pages from
your printer manual showing the
details of its graphics mode I
may be able to alter our own
screen dump routine - Brian]

From: Douglas Goldsworthy


Is it possible to find out (from
E.M. Duffield (Outlet 10) or
elsewhere) how the Wafadrive I/O
instructions should be modified
from those given in the Wafa-
drive manual.

I bought my Wafadrive primarily
for use as a driver for my
Centronics HR5 - so far without
success. The Wafadrive works.The
printer works on my Atmos and
the cable is new!


       Douglas Goldsworthy

>Douglas Goldsworthy from Brian

Do you get anything at all from
the Wafadrive to the HR5? Is the
HR5 both Centronics and RS232
like the M1009?If so,you'll need
to alter the dipswitch setting
in the printer if you have been
using RS232 from the Atmos.

If you get no response at all
from your printer when trying to
print from the Wafadrive I would
supect the cable is not wired up
correctly for the Wafa (I assume
there are variations) or there
is a fault in the output wiring
from the Wafadrive.What does the
Wafadrive manual actually say on
initializing a printer to LPRINT
etc?
                      - Brian

From E.J. Chun,   Lancs.

Dear Ron & Brian,

Congratulations on the anniver-
sary of OUTLET. It does not seem
like a year has gone past (Well,
nearly a year as I came in on
Issue 3). Time moves on very
quickly for those of us who are
over forty. I have been finally
tempted to put fingers on
keyboad to write my first leter
to any computer publication so
you can see the influence you
have had on me. I have found
OUTLET to be of great value and
it has rekindled my interest in
USING my computer as a tool and
not a games machine. Though I
must admit I still enjoy many of

my games collection. I found out
very early that I would not make
a programmer,only a key-puncher.
Keep up the good work for many
more years.

However,I can now give an answer
to a query from one of your
readers.It's from Andrew Clapham
in the July,No.11 Issue, regard-
ing programs for cassette label
printing. I have come across two
of them.

1.  OCTOBER 1986 - ZX COMPUTING
    MONTHLY  (I ENCLOSE A PHOTO-
    COPY IF YOU CAN SEND IT ON).

2.  ISSUE 22 - 16/48 COMPUTING.
    (I would have done a print-
out but my printer is not behav-

ing itself). This one does cass-
ette labels, cassette inserts as
well as video labels and I have
found it to be excellent. I have
always thought that 16/48
COMPUTING and the other tape
magazine SPECTRUM COMPUTING have
been much maligned. I personally
thought that they were good
value and had a great deal of
useful information in them.Don't
forget that they were a quick
introduction to home computing
for a great many people. I still
go through them for some of the
utility programs that appeared
in them.

That seems to be it for the time
being. Best wishes for many more
issues.

        Yours sincerely,

            E.J. Chun

P.S. The annual index is a very
good idea but surely once a year
is better than updating each
month?

To. E.J. Chun from Brian
Thanks for your good wishes and
the info. Ron tells me he's now
passed on the photocopy to
Andrew. I too enjoyed the old
tape mags though towards the end
at `3.99 each, I only bought one
if It appeared to have something
of interest. Four to five years
ago (yes it's that long ago) `4
was worth more than today and I
felt it was just a quid over the
barrier of hesitancy for many. I
think, with hind-sight,they were
good value. I enjoyed them and
still use some of the programs
like the graphics program: PAD
16/48. I must have had `20's
worth of use out of that one
program! As for the index data,
what do other people think about
just putting it in once a year?

From: Anthony Poli, Preston

Dear Ron & Brian,

It is nice to be operational
again,after my system breakdown.

Has anybody found out what prod-
uces the: 3 subscript wrong
9996:5. On 'ZAP' when using the
print option? It is annoying me.

I have just got my 2nd drive
back after having it fixed. It
only saves if the cartridge was
formatted in drive 1 but it will
not load and produces "file not
found". If you try formatting a
cartridge and CAT in drive 1
there is only 4K free on it. I
have sent it back and they

showed it working but I have
tried without drive 1 and still
it does not work. So if anyone
can help please do or does
anyone want to give me an offer?

I bet your thinking, "How much
more can I take of this!". Many
thanks for a great magazine.

         Yours sincerely

               A. POLI

To Anthony Poli from Brian

I think some mdrives/i'faces are
incompatible with one another. I
cannot FORMAT reliably on my 2nd
drive and sometimes a CAT and
LOAD will miss files which are
picked up by drive 1. I suspect
it's because tolerances in the
quality control were too wide.

Sorry about ZAP! To correct the
fault, load ZAP from Issue 9
(Cartridge A), put Cartridge A
from this issue (13) in drive 1,
BREAK into ZAP and type:

     MERGE*"m";1;"ZAPMOD2"

Enter RUN 9980 to re-SAVE the
program. This is the 2nd MOD for
ZAP due to my stupidity! - Brian

From: Mr. E.M. Duffield, Crawley

Dear Ron & Brian,

Thank you for issues up to 12. I
have no criticisms and I partic-
ularly liked the mobile graphic
programs a couple of issues
back. I showed them to the great
grand children and they stopped
fidgeting and didn't make a
sound. I wonder why?

I seem to remember a few issues
ago, one of your readers
enquiring about the One-Per-Desk
double microdrive Units. Well
with the aid of a cheap volt
meter I have discovered the
connections. [Details should be
in next month - BC]

At the recent ZX Microfair I
bought a broken 128K machine for
`25. As the 4-R-V keys were
doing peculiar things, it helped
me to find the short - caused no
doubt by a minute piece of
solder under the ULA holder.
However the TV picture is very
poor, there being vertical
Yellows or Blues attached to a
black and white picture. But the
128 has a RGB output so although
my monitor cannot distinguish
between normal and Bright, the
graphics programs are marvelous.

If any of your readers has a
program that will import into
the 128K I would be very inter-
ested.The PRINT instruction uses
the output port of the Sound

chip AY-3-8912 but the Manual
gives very little information on
the output side.

Some time ago I had given up one
of these chips as lost but while
taking voltage readings it sudd-
enly burst into life. Later I
realized that I had earthed the
reset pin (16).

If you manage to find a way of
transferring Outlet to MGT + D
discs I would be willing to acc-
ept them in lieu of cartridges.
My 5.25" are only 40 tracks DS
the 3.5" is 80 tracks DS.

Thanking you in anticipation.

          E M Duffield

To E.M. Duffield from Brian

Many thanks for the OPD m/drive
units and conversion to Spectrum
info which I shall try to get in
next month's DRIVECHAT. Great
stuff!I'll add my "test report"!

Glad you liked the graphics. Was
that ARNOLD or CARPET WEAVER in
#10 or maybe WINDOWINDER in #11?
Re:the monitor,it reminded me of
CARPET WEAVER's title page and
also the carpet backgrounds.They
have CARPET WEAVER spelt out in
BRIGHT squares.I realized later
the words are invisible to
anyone with a monitor!

Outlet IS available on +D. I'll
ask Ron to send you a disk or to
contact you if a problem. -Brian.

## КАК НАПИСАТЬ В OUTLET

Письма для публикации в нашей рубрике OUTLETTERS принимаются практически в любом виде: в операторах BASIC PRINT или DATA, на рукописных или отпечатанных на машинке страницах; простая программа JOTTER прилагается в Выпуске 2 (Диск #4); сообщения на почтовый ящик через Prestel № 014703943. Однако проще всего нам редактировать файлы Tasword 2 с правым полем, установленным на 32.

Пожалуйста, укажите, если в вашем письме есть части, которые вы не хотите публиковать, хотя мы в любом случае действуем по своему усмотрению. Письма также могут быть отредактированы для ясности и сокращения... Пожалуйста, напишите, если вы не против прямой переписки с другими читателями OUTLET, и мы опубликуем ваш полный адрес.

### От John Luby, Duns

Дорогие Ron/Brian,

Ещё несколько советов для владельцев 128K (совершенно бесплатно — это не я изобрёл). В прошлый раз я упоминал о том, как редактор 128K пытается «токенизировать» всё, что похоже на «зарезервированное слово» (т.е. команду или функцию). Имейте в виду: он делает обратное, когда текст заключён в кавычки. Строка вида:

```text
 LET p = VAL "PEEK 23606 + 256 * PEEK 23607"
```

вообще не будет работать, если ввести её в режиме 128. Если же ввести её в режиме 48K, она будет работать в 128K — до тех пор, пока вы не решите её отредактировать, и в этот момент редактор ДЕтокенизирует всё, что находится внутри кавычек.

Кроме того, «внедрённые» коды управления цветом в режиме 128K недоступны. Строки из 48K со встроенными атрибутами БУДУТ работать (хотя эффекта в листингах 128K не видно). Однако стоит отредактировать строку — и коды исчезнут. Если вы программируете в режиме 128K, атрибуты приходится задавать «по старинке» (`PRINT PAPER 2; INK 7` и т.д.).

И последнее: табуляция листингов или текста с помощью `<EXTEND>`, `<6>`, `<DELETE>` исключена, если вы хотите просматривать их в 128K. `CHR$ 6` творит с листингами 128K ужасные вещи, в некоторых случаях приводя к зависанию. Придётся вернуться к использованию REM для форматирования листингов и пробелов в вашем тексте! (А вы-то наверняка думали, что экранный редактор 128K — это шаг вперёд!).

Прошу прощения за ошибку в ZAP! Чтобы исправить её, загрузите ZAP из Выпуска 9 (Картридж A), вставьте Картридж A из этого выпуска (13) в дисковод 1, прервите выполнение ZAP по нажатию BREAK и введите:

```text
MERGE *"m";1;"ZAPMOD2"
```

Затем введите `RUN 9980`, чтобы повторно сохранить (SAVE) программу. Это уже 2-я модификация для ZAP, возникшая по моей глупости! — Brian
